mission_10: Ensemble forecasting combines predictions from multiple models to produce more accurate and robust forecasts than any individual model. The fundamental insight is that different models capture different aspects of the data generating process, and their errors tend to be uncorrelated, so averaging reduces overall prediction variance. Simple averaging is surprisingly effective and serves as a strong baseline. Weighted averaging allows you to assign more importance to better-performing models based on historical accuracy. The median ensemble is robust to outlier predictions from poorly performing models. Trimmed mean ensembles discard the most extreme forecasts before averaging, combining robustness with efficiency. Variance-weighted ensembles assign higher weights to models with lower prediction variance, reflecting greater confidence in stable forecasts. Stacking learns optimal combination weights by minimizing forecast error on a validation set using gradient descent with projection onto the probability simplex. Bootstrap aggregation (bagging) generates an ensemble by repeatedly resampling the training data, fitting models to each bootstrap sample, and aggregating their predictions, naturally providing prediction intervals from the distribution of bootstrap forecasts. In this mission, you will implement all these ensemble strategies, completing your time series forecasting toolkit.
